title: TROP2 targeting reveals therapy-driven cell state dynamics in colorectal cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all files in the 7 ArrayExpress studies (E-MTAB-16583/16585/16433/16849/16843/16836/16835) via the BioStudies API and downloaded and parsed 9 per-cell metadata tables plus a feature list and a multiplexing reference (no login). Verified cell counts: 785 and 6,429 (patient tissue), 10,135 (patient-derived xenograft epithelium, 24 samples, 7 donors), 7,330 (drug vs vehicle xenografts, 8 mice), 44,779 (in-vivo drug time course, 19 samples, one line HD4246), 46,906 (in-vitro organoid time course, 16 samples, one line), 2,727 (chemotherapy organoid LM2), 1,573 (mouse tumours, 6 mice). Read the first line of a count matrix over FTP: plain tab-delimited dense text, genes as rows, cell barcodes as columns. Read the authors' GitHub code (utils_biobank_subcut.py, utils_SG_timecourse.py) showing the cell-state names are a hand-made dictionary mapping Leiden cluster numbers to labels.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 246-patient case-control cohort and the stage II survival cohort with TROP2 immunostaining (Supplementary Tables 1-2) were read in the text only; the Europe PMC supplementary-file listing timed out and was not retrieved. Sequencing chemistry, Cell Ranger version, Harmony integration and Palantir trajectory settings come from the Methods text.

a1_downloadable.note: All 7 ArrayExpress/BioStudies accessions are public and open; I downloaded metadata files and streamed a count-matrix header with no login or application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Experiment-design labels (drug, timepoint, replicate, donor_id, site, line) are real columns in the released per-cell metadata. The paper's headline label, the named cell state (ISC, revSC, Fetal/HRC, DTP), is NOT a column but is a one-line map from the released Leiden cluster number using a dictionary in the authors' GitHub.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression matrices (raw counts and author log1p-normalised) are present as dense tab-delimited text with 27,185 gene symbols, not accession stubs; verified the header of biobank_tissue_epi_counts.txt.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are unambiguous: unique-molecule counts in the *_counts.txt files, log1p counts-per-10k in *_counts_log1p.txt, hours in the timepoint column; file naming and Methods agree.

a5_enough_rows.note: Cells are plentiful but biological units are not. Every therapy time course comes from ONE patient-derived line (HD4246 for all sacituzumab govitecan data; HD4347 for chemotherapy), the drug-vs-vehicle arm is 8 mice, and the only multi-donor set is 10,135 xenograft cells from 7 donors plus 785 epithelial cells from patient tissue. No held-out-donor evaluation is possible, so this is A5-in-disguise exactly as in the scCT-DB precedent.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1-2 GB after converting one dense text matrix to a sparse object; the full collection is >50 GB and includes a 23.4 GB imputed CSV that must be skipped.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Feasible only after a one-off streaming conversion of 1.2-5 GB dense text matrices; verified file sizes from the BioStudies API.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts in the downloaded metadata match the figure legends exactly: 10,135 cells / 7 donors, 7,330 cells / 4 tumours per arm, 1,573 cells / 3 mice per genotype.

a8_label_provenance.note: The cell-state label that the whole paper is about is a Leiden clustering of the same expression matrix, renamed by eye from marker genes (verified in utils_biobank_subcut.py). Predicting it from expression is circular — leakage by construction. Only the drug/timepoint columns have provenance outside the features.

existing_models.name: scGPT (single-cell transcriptome foundation model)
existing_models.score_and_split: From retrieved search summaries of a 2025 Nature Methods benchmark and the scPerturBench study (27 methods, 29 datasets): deep perturbation-response models including scGPT did not beat a simple mean-of-training-examples baseline on held-out perturbations. I read the search summaries, not the full papers.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Benchmark authors name generalisation to unseen cell contexts and unseen perturbations as still unsolved.

existing_models.name: Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome foundation model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Same retrieved benchmark summaries report it leads on ranking gene importance but not on absolute expression change; no split numbers verified by me.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer to new tissues and new drugs.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome foundation models); both have open weights and could embed these cells
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop for a frozen-embedding plus logistic-regression head on ~90,000 cells, slow but possible
backbone.licence: scGPT MIT; Geneformer Apache-2.0; the data itself is EMBL-EBI open under the ArrayExpress terms

integration.partner_dataset: The Cancer Genome Atlas colon adenocarcinoma bulk expression (TCGA-COAD, 468 tumours) and public colorectal single-cell atlases, joinable on HGNC gene symbol
integration.join_key: gene symbol (no per-cell key exists to join on)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do therapy-induced fetal-like cell states defined in one patient's organoids appear in bulk tumours of other patients — a question that cannot be answered honestly here because the single-cell side rests on one or two patients.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: the drug arm must be recoverable at late timepoints, since the paper shows large composition shifts by 48-120 h; also predicting total counts per cell from the matrix as a plumbing check.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling and shuffling within hashtag sample would run, and the within-sample shuffle is essential because every condition is its own hashtag batch.
controls.external_validation: Weak: the in-vitro and in-vivo time courses are the same patient line, and the chemotherapy course is a different drug in a different patient, so no independent-donor test set exists.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained on this data could only claim: within one patient-derived colorectal cancer line, a cell's transcriptome indicates which antibody-drug conjugate it received and roughly how many hours ago — a claim that cannot be separated from the hashtag batch that encodes the same condition.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a tumour cell's gene-expression profile to predict which drug it received and how many hours ago.
plain_idea.train_on: Single-cell gene-expression profiles (27,185 genes per cell) from colorectal cancer organoids treated with the TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate sacituzumab govitecan or a non-targeting control: 46,906 cells in a dish across 16 samples and 44,779 cells from mouse liver metastases across 19 samples, all from one patient-derived line (verified in the metadata files).
plain_idea.predict: The treatment arm and the hours since dosing. The truth comes from the experiment itself: each condition was labelled with a barcode tag (hashtag) at harvest and recorded in the released metadata as drug/timepoint columns.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer-pharmacology labs would learn whether a drug-response signature read off organoids in a dish transfers to tumours growing in an animal; here it cannot be answered, because the only data come from one or two patients and each condition is confounded with its own batch.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a classifier on single-cell expression to recover drug arm (TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate vs non-targeting control) and hours on treatment, then test transfer from organoids in a dish to liver metastases in mice. Dies because all sacituzumab govitecan data come from one patient-derived line, every condition is its own barcode-tag batch, and the paper's real label (named cell states) is a clustering of the same expression matrix.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: converting a 5 GB dense text matrix (27,185 genes x 44,779 cells) to a sparse object by streaming rows is a few hours of wall clock and ~8 GB peak; a frozen single-cell foundation-model embedding of ~90,000 cells on CPU is roughly a day; a logistic-regression head cross-validates in minutes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count distinct donors behind each time course. The answer is one (HD4246 for every sacituzumab govitecan experiment, HD4347 for chemotherapy) — a 30-second check in the metadata files that kills the project.

verdict_reason: Beautiful, fully open single-cell resource (7 ArrayExpress studies, >120,000 cells, reproducible code), but it fails A5 and A8. The nominal row count is cells; the biological unit is the patient, and every therapy time course comes from one patient-derived line (HD4246), with 8 mice in the drug-vs-vehicle arm and 7 donors in the only multi-donor set. The paper's central label, the named cell state, is a Leiden clustering of the very expression matrix that would be the model input, so predicting it is circular. The only non-circular labels, drug and timepoint, are perfectly confounded with the hashtag batch and cannot be validated on an independent donor.
